description: Authoritative writer/owner registry for every table in ops.* schema. Lints against architecture/schema-snapshot.json. See architecture/README.md.

writers.name: ap-bill-inbox
writers.schedule: event-driven (Resend inbound email webhook) + on-demand reprocess
external_inputs: Resend receiving API (attachment reads — needs a FULL-ACCESS key, RESEND_INBOUND_API_KEY)
writers.notes: The AP bill inbox. bills@alamedapointbg.com -> bill-email-intake.mjs (Svix-gated on RESEND_AP_INBOX_SECRET; Resend mints a separate signing secret per webhook endpoint, so this cannot share the vendor route's) -> bill-email-process-background.mjs reads the attachment, OCRs it with the same extractor human uploads use, and lands an UNPAID BILL DRAFT tagged 'AP Inbox' with the PDF attached. It NEVER posts to QuickBooks: an emailed bill from outside the company must not be able to create a QBO transaction, so every draft waits for a human 'Post to QuickBooks' click (expense-request-link-bill), per the 2026-08-14 gate. Every failure is a visible, re-runnable status on ops.bill_email_intake, and 'no attachment' is kept distinct from 'could not read the attachment' because those have different fixes. Reviewed in Brixpense at /expense/bills via bills-inbox.mjs (staff-only). Config in ops.expense_settings key 'ap_inbox'. Tables: migration 20260823024339_bill_email_intake.sql. Duplicate guard: ops.fn_bill_duplicate_candidates (exact = vendor+bill_number; likely = vendor+amount within 10 days, discounted when both rows carry DIFFERENT job numbers) stamps expense_requests.duplicate_of/_reason/_checked_at at intake and is re-checked in expense-request-link-bill, which refuses (409 possible_duplicate) only when the twin is already in QuickBooks; an override is recorded in duplicate_cleared_by. Due dates: OCR extracts due_date + payment_terms separately, ops.fn_due_date_from_terms (mirrored in netlify/functions/lib/due-date.mjs and app-expense/src/lib/dueDate.ts, pinned by tests/due-date.test.mjs) derives one when only terms are printed, and ops.v_ap_aging buckets what is unpaid.

writers.name: brixpense:bill-rules
writers.schedule: event-driven (applied during AP-inbox bill intake) + staff edits
writers.notes: Auto-populate rules for inbound bills. expense-rules.mjs is the CRUD + dry-run endpoint; lib/expense-rules.mjs is the pure matcher (case-insensitive substring, inclusive amount bounds, ALL conditions must hold, lowest priority wins — no regex, deliberately inspectable). bill-email-process-background applies the winning rule to a new bill and stamps expense_requests.applied_rule_id so 'why is this account on here' is answerable, then records match_count/last_matched_at/last_amount on the rule. A rule fills BLANKS: what OCR read off the document (vendor, amount, date) always wins. ⚠ A rule NEVER posts to QuickBooks — the 2026-08-14 human gate is not something a config row may bypass. Read: anyone in Brixpense (ops.fn_has_brixpense); write: staff.

writers.name: brixpense:expense-books
writers.notes: Expense report books. A book bundles ops.expense_requests rows ACROSS payment types (card, check, emailed bill, SF job expense) and ties them to a tag/job/period; totals break out by payment type, GL account and entity via ops.v_expense_book_totals. Membership is explicit rather than a saved filter — the point is grouping things a filter cannot express. Books never mutate the expenses they contain; deleting a book only drops the memberships. CSV export prefix-quotes leading =+-@ so an OCR'd vendor name cannot become a live formula in Excel. Read: anyone in Brixpense; write: the book's creator or staff (RLS).

writers.name: vendor-email-intake
writers.notes: Vendor email → SF ticket automation. Red Bull (rbfreeflow@) and Freshpet (freshpet@) emails are parsed by Claude and become SF jobs under the route's sf_customer_name; SF's own job-status notification emails (pointed at sf-status@) are parsed and relayed to the route's send_list. Intake + confirm gate are event-driven; status relays come from BOTH the sf-status@ email trigger and the 5-min vendor-ticket-status-poll (shared applyStatusChange pipeline, deduped on last_sf_status). Svix-signature gated (RESEND_INBOUND_SECRET). Source: netlify/functions/vendor-email-intake.mjs; tables seeded by migration 20260722a.

writers.name: vendor-ticket-status-poll
writers.notes: Safety-net status poller for vendor tickets — SF's notification emails proved unreliable as the sole status signal (2026-07-22). Walks open sf_created tickets (cap 25/tick, terminal invoiced/cancelled, 60-day age-out), reads each SF job, and relays status changes via the shared applyStatusChange pipeline in vendor-email-intake.mjs (event row + templated update email). Deduped on last_sf_status so the email trigger and poller can never double-send.

writers.name: pricing-admin
writers.notes: Pricing Control Center editor (superadmin). Service-role REST against the ops pricing model: BX-1 standard book (effective-dated price_book_items), customer price-book assignment, and named/dated chain contracts. Read by brix-order via ops.resolve_price / ops.resolve_prices_for_customer (contract -> BX-1 -> list). Source: netlify/functions/pricing-admin.mjs.

writers.name: qbo-cylinder-audit
writers.notes: Source at supabase/functions/qbo-cylinder-audit/. Creates the $0 CR-ADJ-<n> cylinder audit adjustment invoice in QBO (cylinder delivery items for count-up deltas, PU* pickup items for count-down) for brix-order's audit-submit function (x-internal-secret == INTERNAL_PAY_SECRET, verify_jwt=false), then immediately upserts the header + lines into the ops mirror (same conflict keys as sync-qbo) so brix-order's v_cylinder_inventory reflects the adjustment instantly. Token via lease RPCs.

writers.name: qbo-reconcile
external_inputs: QuickBooks Online API (active invoice IDs by window)
writers.notes: Source at supabase/functions/qbo-reconcile/. PRUNES mirror invoices QBO no longer returns (deleted in QBO) so they stop ghosting in brix-order. Guarded: dry-run by default (mode=prune to delete), prune requires INTERNAL_PAY_SECRET OR a service-role bearer, per-type 0-result guard, global max_prune cap, paginated mirror read. Emails a Resend report (RECONCILE_REPORT_TO/_FROM) only when it prunes or aborts. Daily backstop cron 'qbo-reconcile-daily' (09:20 UTC, 150-day window) is created DISABLED until INTERNAL_PAY_SECRET is dropped into its header. Complements qbo-webhook's real-time Delete-event prune.

writers.name: qbo-webhook
writers.notes: Source at supabase/functions/qbo-webhook/. verify_jwt=false; auth is Intuit's HMAC signature (QBO_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN). On an Invoice/Payment change, re-reads the affected invoice(s) from QBO and updates qbo_invoices balance/status in real time so brix-order flips to Paid within seconds. Writes qbo_token_cache via lease RPC. Requires Intuit dashboard webhook config to fire.

writers.name: sync-qbo
writers.schedule: called by qbo-sync-runner (Netlify scheduled function every 5 min)
writers.notes: Source at supabase/functions/sync-qbo/. Writes qbo_token_cache via lease RPC ops.qbo_token_claim_refresh(). v45 logs mv_sales_lines refreshes and treats QBO HTTP/Fault responses as failures instead of empty success. Direct pg_cron callers are disabled by 20260703j; qbo-sync-runner holds Supabase auth in Netlify env and calls this Edge Function.

writers.notes: Populates purchase_cost which powers est_cost / est_margin in v_sales_lines. Uses lease RPC for token refresh. v8 now writes qbo:items sync_log rows. The old direct pg_cron caller is disabled by 20260703j.

writers.name: qbo-sync-runner
writers.notes: Scheduler bridge at netlify/functions/qbo-sync-runner.mjs. Holds Supabase bearer auth in Netlify runtime env instead of SQL cron text, computes rolling offsets from ops.sync_log, and calls the existing Supabase Edge Functions only when invoices, missing-line backfill, edited-line refresh, materialized-view refresh, or qbo_items are stale.

It never deletes customers and blocks rows with open AR, recent revenue, future invoices, or missing Service Fusion match.

writers.name: geocode-customers

writers.notes: Source at supabase/functions/geocode-customers/. writers.name: brix-expense:app-and-functions
writers.schedule: on-demand (user submits expense / manager approves / link-bill)
writers.notes: Brixpense surface (app-expense/ Vite SPA at /expense/ + netlify/functions/expense-request-* + expense-to-bill + process-inbound). Frontend uses anon key under permissive RLS (submitters INSERT/UPDATE own rows; anon SELECT/UPDATE gated on approval_token presence for the magic-link approval page). Netlify functions use the anon key bound to the user JWT or service role for cross-cutting status transitions, approval logging, and QBO bill creation. expense_settings is read by useExpenseSettings(); seeded by 20260512_create_expense_tables.sql (auto_approve_threshold + approval_email) and finished by 20260512p_expense_cleanup.sql (cogs_accounts + manager_emails + tags + corrected departments). expense-cc-match (Master Control → Card & Expense Match) links/imports QBO Purchase card-feed transactions into ops.expense_requests (qbo_purchase_id columns, migration 20260715000001). **No expense auto-posts to QuickBooks (2026-08-14).** expense-request-notify's 'expense' branch now ONLY auto-approves (draft→approved, no manager workflow — unchanged) and never calls QBO. expense-request-link-bill is the one place a human explicitly posts (mode=create) — handles BOTH the unpaid-Bill case (as_bill=true, vendor must match a QBO vendor) and the paid-Purchase case (as_bill=false, needs payment_account_id; Purchase support is new here, moved from expense-request-notify) — writes status=posted/qbo_bill_id/vendor_id/posted_at, attaches receipts, flips a linked PR to fulfilled, computes margin-match. Frontend surfaces the click: ExpenseForm's success screen ('Post to QuickBooks' button right after Submit), PendingList ('My Submissions', per-row button on any approved expense not yet posted), SFExpenses (same, for SF-tag rows). The sf-expense-autopost-background pg_cron job is UNSCHEDULED (migration 20260814000001) — the function itself is left in place as a superadmin-gated manual escape hatch only, nothing calls it automatically; its ops.sync_health() check was dropped (was destined to sit permanently red). sf-expense-ocr-background (daily pg_cron 10:15 UTC) is UNCHANGED and still useful: it runs the shared Claude OCR (netlify/functions/lib/expense-ocr-core.mjs, also used by the interactive expense-ocr.mjs upload flow) against each SF-tag draft's attached receipt, writes ops.expense_request_attachments.ocr_result (jsonb — declared since 20260512_create_expense_tables.sql, unused until 2026-08-13) + promotes bill_number/ocr_status/ocr_processed_at/ocr_error/ocr_notified_at onto ops.expense_requests (migration 20260813000002) so a human reviewing an SF draft sees a pre-filled bill number and a 'Needs review — …' badge when the receipt/OCR/bill-number is missing. bill_number → QBO Bill.DocNumber (capped 21 chars) on both Bill and Purchase payloads in expense-request-link-bill. **Editable-after-approval + failure notification (2026-08-14):** an SF-landed draft with a bad receipt_date (one carried a literal 2020-08-04 from historical SF data) hit QBO error 6210 'Account Period Closed' on post, and the edit form was read-only once status left 'draft', so there was no way to fix it. expense-request-notify now accepts resubmission from 'draft' OR 'approved' for request_type='expense' (re-validates + re-approves, doesn't require a fresh draft); app-expense/ExpenseForm.tsx unlocks editing for 'approved' rows accordingly (still locked once 'posted'). expense-request-link-bill now extracts the actual QBO Fault message (was surfacing the raw JSON blob) and — on ANY failure to post (QBO error, no vendor match, no payment account) — stamps `autopost_error` on the row and emails REPORT_TO, so a failed post is visible without depending on whoever clicked it noticing; PendingList/SFExpenses show that reason inline. card-receipt-audit-background (weekly Mon 15:00 UTC pg_cron) audits QBO card Purchases vs expense_requests receipts and emails the missing list; writes ops.sync_log only. expense-cc-match also owns ops.expense_card_map (card last-4 → cardholder/user map for company-card attribution, migration 20260724000005; assign/unassign from Master Control → Card & Expense Match → Cardholders).

writers.name: sf-receipt-pull
writers.schedule: every 30 min via Supabase pg_cron (synchronous; cronKey)
writers.notes: Synchronous SF receipt puller — scans recent completed/invoiced SF jobs, lands each receipt as a Brixpense review-DRAFT via lib/sf-expense.landSfJobExpense (scan + attach, no QBO post). Reuses the in-runtime SF auth (single token owner). Returns full diagnostics to the caller. Deduped by sf_expense_id; gated to SF_SWEEP_START_DATE. Replaces the invisible background sweep.

writers.name: sf-receipt-sync
writers.schedule: Supabase pg_cron: crawl every 10 min + fresh (newest 5 pages) every 15 min
writers.notes: Edge-function replacement for the Netlify sf-receipt-pull/sf-expense-sweep pair (chosen for reliable scheduling + visible ops.sync_log). Pages SF status=Invoiced jobs and lands each expense as a Brixpense review-DRAFT (status='draft', as_bill, tag='Service Fusion', qbo_bill_id NULL — NOTHING posts to QBO; Brixpense posts on submit). SWEEP SORTS (v22, 2026-08-14): the fresh sweep pages by sort=-updated_at — adding/editing an SF expense bumps the JOB's updated_at, so an expense added to a months-old already-Invoiced job surfaces on page 1 within one sweep cycle (sorted by -id it sat hundreds of jobs deep and was never revisited — 12 expenses/~$9k missed that way incl. both DESERT BEVERAGE jobs); the historical crawl keeps the stable sort=-id walk. Vendor = SF expense.purchased_from. RECEIPT IMAGE: SF's REST API exposes the expense LINE but not the receipt file; the receipt S3 URL lives only on the admin.servicefusion.com job page, so we resolve the job number -> encrypted admin id via POST /serviceSpot/loadGlobalSearchResults, GET /jobs/jobView?id=<enc>, scrape the servicefusion.s3.amazonaws.com/userdocs/<co>/jobexpense/... URL, and fetch it from public S3 (anon). The admin portal uses the orders.sf_portal_session cookie; when stale the function auto-refreshes it by GETting SF_PORTAL_REFRESH_HOOK (the Make login hook) and upserting the parsed cookie back into orders.sf_portal_session. Dedup by sf_expense_id (synthetic key when SF gives no expense id); receipts backfill onto existing drafts that have no attachment. gateByDate on SF_SWEEP_START_DATE in sweep mode. Reuses sync-sf's SF auth via ops.sf_token_cache and the shared refresh lease from 20260704a so Edge and Netlify callers do not rotate the same refresh token concurrently. createClient { db:{schema:'ops'} }; reads/writes orders.sf_portal_session via .schema('orders'). Shares the table with the Brixpense surface + resq-sf-sync (all multi_writer).

writers.name: sf-expense-sweep-background
writers.schedule: deprecated (invisible background fn — superseded by sf-receipt-pull)
writers.notes: Deprecated in favor of the synchronous sf-receipt-pull. Same landSfJobExpense delegation; kept declared while the file exists.

writers.name: brix-stock:app-and-rpcs
writers.notes: Multi-writer with sub-distributors:app-and-rpcs (2026-08-18) — both write transfers/lines/movements exclusively through the same SECURITY DEFINER RPC family, so the ledger stays append-only and single-pathed. BRIX Stock surface (app/src/pages/stock/) writes via ops.fn_create_transfer / fn_ship_transfer / fn_receive_transfer / fn_void_transfer (all SECURITY DEFINER, authenticated only). inventory_movements is append-only via those RPCs; clients never INSERT directly. inventory_locations is directly writable from the UI under permissive RLS (low volume CRUD; virtual TRANSIT and ADJUSTMENT rows are protected by a kind-NOT-IN check in the update policy). Phase 1 only emits transfer_ship and transfer_receive movement types; Phase 4 will add receipt (from bills) and shipment (from invoices). See architecture/PRODUCT-CONTROL.md for the full design. Migration: 20260513a_inventory_stock.sql.

writers.name: sub-distributors:app-and-rpcs
writers.schedule: on-demand (Refractor Sub-Distributors page + the /distributor partner portal)
writers.notes: Sub-distributor program (Origins Soda Co., Desert Beverage → The Melt/Starbird territories). Staff manage the registry/agreements/accounts from Refractor → Sub-Distributors under fn_is_staff RLS; distributor logins (ops.sub_distributor_users, matched by user_id or JWT email) act ONLY through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs: fn_distributor_create_order / fn_distributor_cancel_order / fn_fulfill_distributor_order (staff) / fn_distributor_receive_transfer (per-line counts; shortfall stays in TRANSIT + has_discrepancy flag) / fn_distributor_sign_agreement / fn_distributor_record_depletion (posts 'shipment' movements out of the distributor location + consignment fee snapshot). Transfer/movement writes ride the same RPC ledger as brix-stock (hence multi_writer). External access is scoped by AS RESTRICTIVE policies added in the same migration — distributor logins are narrowed to their own slice across ~100 previously open-read ops tables. Migration: 20260818f_sub_distributors.sql. PHASE 2 (20260820a): fee settlement — fn_distributor_settlement_create (staff) sweeps un-settled fee-carrying depletions into ops.sub_distributor_settlements and creates a Brixpense expense request (ops.expense_requests, status=approved, as_bill, tag=Sub-Distributor, vendor from the new sub_distributors.qbo_vendor_id link) so QBO posting stays behind Brixpense's human Post-to-QuickBooks gate (multi-writer on expense_requests with brixpense); fn_distributor_settlement_void releases depletions + archives the unposted request. Agreements gain scope + signer_ip/signer_user_agent (sign RPC reads request.headers).

writers.name: distributor-notify
writers.schedule: Netlify scheduled function every 15 min (+ on-demand staff kick)
writers.notes: Sub-distributor notification scan: order_submitted → staff (DISTRIBUTOR_ALERT_TO, default service@brixbev.com), order_fulfilled + transfer_shipped → partner (contact_email ∪ active portal users), transfer received with discrepancy → staff, agreement_sent → partner with the portal sign link, agreement_signed → both. Exactly-once via UNIQUE(event_type, ref_id) on ops.sub_distributor_notifications (failed sends recorded and retried next tick); scans capped to the last 30 days so a fresh deploy can never blast history. Service-role only table. Every run logs to ops.sync_log (source 'distributor', sync_type 'distributor_notify') feeding the distributor_notify check in ops.fn_sync_health_extra (yellow >2h, red >12h or logged error — added 20260820b). Source: netlify/functions/distributor-notify.mjs; table from migration 20260820a.

writers.name: brix-compliance:app
writers.schedule: on-demand (Compliance & Safety app at /compliance; legacy vault UI in Refractor → Production)
writers.notes: Compliance & Safety vault: our documents + third-party (vendor/contractor) documents, the SDS library, the training log, the required workplace-postings board, and the signed safety-handbook acknowledgments. Primary UI is now the standalone app public/compliance.html (served at alamedapointbg.com/compliance) — full CRUD straight from the browser over PostgREST under ops.fn_is_staff() RLS, with file upload/replace/download against the private staff-gated bucket compliance-docs (documents/*, sds/*, postings/*, training/*). The Refractor tab app/src/pages/production/ComplianceTab.tsx still writes the same tables. compliance-expiry-cron.mjs (Mondays 15:30 UTC) is read-only — emails an expired/expiring-≤60d digest to COMPLIANCE_ALERT_TO (default service@brixbev.com). compliance_postings.short_title is the label the one-page TV board uses (a 65-inch screen affords about two lines per notice); mirror_path names a copy of the notice committed to public/postings/ and served at /billing/postings/<file>, which is what the board renders on a monitor (agency hosts refuse to be framed); a staff upload to the bucket takes precedence over it. compliance_postings additionally carries a SELECT-to-authenticated policy and postings/* in the bucket is readable by any signed-in employee (migration 20260818b) — required workplace notices are public by law and the Posting board is the screen employees read them on. safety_handbook_acks is insert-self-only / read-own-or-staff and has no UPDATE or DELETE policy — acknowledgments are immutable. Migrations: 20260726a_compliance_docs.sql, 20260817a_compliance_sds_training.sql, 20260817b_safety_handbook_acks.sql, 20260817c_compliance_postings.sql, 20260818a_compliance_postings_seed.sql, 20260818b_posting_board_read.sql, 20260818c_posting_mirror.sql, 20260818d_posting_short_title.sql (all applied live). writers.name: brixpense-vendors:app-and-fn
writers.notes: Vendor Portal Phase 1 (architecture/VENDOR-PORTAL-PLAN.md, migration 20260820a_ops_vendors.sql). The Brixpense Vendors pages CRUD ops.vendors directly via PostgREST on the user's bearer under staff-only RLS (vendors_staff_all / ops.fn_is_staff(), both directions), and auto-create the linked ops.insured_parties row when a vendor has none — hence multi_writer with brix-compliance:app on insured_parties. Companion Netlify function expense-vendors.mjs (requireAuth superadmin/admin) handles ONLY the QBO calls: live Vendor search and Vendor create; on create it also self-heals the ops.qbo_vendors mirror row (same-shape upsert as push-qbo-item:vendors, which remains that mirror's primary writer). Payment fields store preference + Venmo/PayPal handle ONLY — bank details never land in this schema; EIN stored as last-4 only. Staff can file a vendor's documents directly from the vendor record (vendor-doc-upload.mjs, staff-gated): drop a W-9, a certificate of insurance or a bill and it classifies the document, runs the matching extractor (lib/vendor-doc-ocr.mjs) and lands it via the SHARED lib/vendor-doc-apply.mjs — the same mapper the vendor's own onboarding link uses, so a form produces the same record whichever door it comes through. A W-9 now populates the STRUCTURED 1099 columns (tax_classification, tin_type, w9_received_at, tax_address); before this the extractor read them and wrote them into a notes sentence, leaving the columns empty and the vendor on the chase list. ⚠ A dropped BILL is read for what it says about the vendor and creates NO expense row — the read is handed to the expense form for a human to file, because a money row must not be a side effect of a drag gesture.

writers.name: sf-changes-report

writers.name: visitor-kiosk
writers.notes: Front-door visitor sign-in. netlify/functions/visitor-signin.mjs and visitor-signout.mjs run on SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY because a visitor cannot authenticate — the page public/visitors.html is deliberately unauthenticated and the tables are closed to anon. Sign-in validates, stores the badge photo in the private visitor-photos bucket, allocates a per-day badge number (V-YYYYMMDD-NNN, unique-constrained with retry), inserts the visit and emails the chosen host plus visitor_settings.notify_emails (VISITOR_ALERT_TO overrides). Photo and notification are best effort and record their own failure so the log shows when nobody was actually told. Staff read, sign-out and settings live in /compliance → Visitors under ops.fn_is_staff() RLS; the on-site list is the evacuation head-count. Migration: 20260818e_visitor_kiosk.sql (applied live).

writers.name: vendor-onboarding:intake-and-chase
writers.schedule: on-demand (public /vendor-onboarding intake + staff vendor-request-docs) + Mondays 15:30 UTC (chase inside compliance-expiry-cron)
writers.notes: Vendor Portal Phase 2 (migration 20260820b_vendor_onboard_tokens.sql). Three service-role surfaces share this writer: vendor-request-docs.mjs (staff mints a one-time link, superadmin/admin), vendor-onboard.mjs (the PUBLIC token-gated intake at /vendor-onboarding — visitor-kiosk posture: the sha256-hashed 14-day token is the gate, all writes service-role), and the Monday chase inside compliance-expiry-cron.mjs (expiring/missing-COI vendors get a fresh docs_refresh link, ≤1/vendor/week, run logged to ops.sync_log source=vendors sync_type=vendor_doc_chase → vendor_doc_chase health check). Files land in the compliance-docs bucket under vendors/<party_id>/; document rows go to ops.compliance_documents (multi_writer with brix-compliance:app). Vendor patches touch w9_status/ein_last4(last-4 ONLY)/legal_name/contact/payment pref+handle/onboard_status — never bank details.

writers.name: vendor-qbo-push
writers.schedule: on-demand (staff clicks Push to QuickBooks on a vendor)
writers.notes: Creates (or links) the QuickBooks Vendor for a Brixpense vendor and attaches their compliance documents — W-9, certificate of insurance — to that QBO vendor record via the Attachable API (POST /v3/company/{realm}/upload, multipart file_metadata_01 + file_content_01; Vendor is a supported AttachableRef entity). The only ops write is stamping vendors.qbo_vendor_id. NEVER creates a second QBO vendor: an existing link is verified by id, then an exact DisplayName match is linked to, and only then is one created — QBO rejects duplicate display names anyway, and a split vendor history is the same failure the W-9 drop guards against. ⚠ A full TIN is never sent: ops.vendors holds ein_last4 only, and a partial TaxIdentifier would LOOK filled in — the whole number is on the W-9 PDF, which is why attaching the document is the load-bearing half. Vendor1099 is set only from an EXPLICIT is_1099 override, never inferred. Attachments are best-effort and reported per file, so one unreadable document cannot lose the vendor push or the others.

writers.name: sf-expense-reconcile
writers.notes: The weekly 'did we see everything?' proof for the SF→Brixpense expense pipeline. Re-reads every SF expense on Invoiced jobs updated in the last 30 days (sort=-updated_at, expand=expenses — the same signal the fresh sweep rides), computes the SAME dedup key as sf-receipt-sync's expenseKey() (⚠ the two MUST change together — candidateKey() in the function header says so), and checks each against ops.expense_requests.sf_expense_id. Stranded expenses are landed on the spot via the edge function's ?landJob= (idempotent, drafts only — the manual-post gate holds; capped at 10 jobs/run) and a digest email goes to SF_RECONCILE_ALERT_TO (default service@brixbev.com) ONLY when something was found — silence is the healthy state. Exists because every landing path is best-effort (budgeted sweeps, SF hangs, filtered emails): 12 expenses/~$9k sat invisible for weeks before 2026-08-14, found only because an operator asked. Its only ops write is the sync_log run row (source 'sf-reconcile', added to the source allow-list in 20260826b — the CHECK silently rejects unknown sources, the v0.5.0 trap); the landings themselves are writes by sf-receipt-sync, the already-declared writer. Watcher: ops.fn_sf_reconcile_health() in fn_sync_health_extra — red on an errored run or >8 days silent; green-with-note before the first run.

writers.name: bill-paid-sync
writers.notes: Asks QuickBooks which posted Brixpense bills have actually been paid. Brixpense only stamps paid_at for payments IT made (vendor-payments:pay-and-webhook); a cheque written in QuickBooks, a Bill Pay run or the bookkeeper's card is invisible here, so without this the bill sits in ops.v_ap_aging forever and keeps offering a Pay button for money already gone. Nothing we mirror answers it — ops.qbo_expense_lines is line-level with no header balance — so it queries the Bill entity per id (two batched read-only queries per run, scoped to posted+unpaid+un-archived rows). Bill.Balance is the answer: 0 = paid (paid_at stamped from the linked BillPayment's real date, NOT now — a bill paid in June must not read as paid today); 0 < balance < total = PARTIAL, recorded on qbo_balance but deliberately NOT marked paid, since it is still owed; a bill QBO does not return is recorded checked with a NULL balance and never marked paid (deleted or voided there is not the same as settled). Read-only against QBO: creates nothing, pays nothing, so the manual button is safe for the AP desk. Scope is Bills only (as_bill=true, 2026-08-26 — posted Purchases were false-flagged as deleted) PLUS credit memos (is_credit), which are asked of the VendorCredit entity: a VendorCredit's Balance is what is still UNAPPLIED, so 0 = fully consumed — asking the wrong entity is the same false-missing bug with the sign flipped. Watcher: ops.fn_bill_paid_sync_health() in fn_sync_health_extra — red on an error in 24h or no run in 48h, yellow on bills QBO no longer returns, and yellow (NOT green) when bills are waiting and the sync has never run.

writers.name: vendor-payments:pay-and-webhook
writers.schedule: on-demand (superadmin Pay / Pay-run click) + Stripe webhook on payout settlement
external_inputs: Stripe Global Payouts API v2 (recipients, outbound payments)
writers.notes: Vendor Portal Phase 3 (migration 20260820c_vendor_payments.sql). vendor-pay.mjs is SUPERADMIN-only and the ONLY initiator — no auto-pay exists: actions stripe_status / stripe_setup (creates the v2 recipient Account + emails Stripe's hosted onboarding link; persists vendors.stripe_recipient_id, the only Stripe datum stored — bank details live with Stripe) / preview / pay (Stripe OutboundPayment) / record (manual venmo/zelle/check/qbo_billpay rails). stripe-payout-webhook.mjs (HMAC-verified, STRIPE_PAYOUT_WEBHOOK_SECRET) settles the ledger on 'posted' and books the QBO BillPayment through the hardened billing token chain; failed/returned/canceled flip to 'failed' and email REPORT_TO. Duplicate protection is a partial unique index on qbo_bill_id for live statuses. Health: ops.fn_vendor_payments_health() inside fn_sync_health_extra (red on a failure in 7d or a payout stuck 'initiated' >48h). Writes ops.vendors only to stamp stripe_recipient_id — multi_writer with brixpense-vendors:app-and-fn and vendor-onboarding:intake-and-chase. Also stamps the BILL itself (ops.expense_requests paid_at / payment_method / qbo_billpayment_id) when a manual rail is recorded or a Stripe payout settles — multi_writer with brix-expense:app-and-functions. The ledger is the payment's story, expense_requests is the bill's, and ops.v_ap_aging keys on paid_at: leave the bill unstamped and a paid bill sits in the aging total forever. PAY RUN (2026-08-26, migration 20260826d): vendor-pay-run.mjs (same superadmin gate) pays SEVERAL bills to one vendor in one action — per-bill ledger rows stay the duplicate guard (written BEFORE any money moves), and a parent ops.vendor_payment_groups row carries what is singular about the batch: the one Stripe payout id (the row-level unique index can't hold when five rows share one payout), the one multi-line QBO BillPayment, the check #, and the remittance-advice send record (lib/remittance.mjs — sent at settlement for Stripe via the webhook's settleGroup(), immediately for manual rails, resendable via action=remit). No new watcher: batch rows are ordinary vendor_payments rows, so fn_vendor_payments_health() already covers a stuck or failed pay run. VENDOR CREDITS (2026-08-26, migration 20260826e): expense_requests.is_credit rows post to QBO as VendorCredit (expense-request-link-bill) and are CONSUMED by applying them in a pay run — the BillPayment gains positive-Amount lines with LinkedTxn TxnType VendorCredit and TotalAmt = bills − credits (never negative; $0 apply-only allowed on the record rail). Credit rows get vendor_payments ledger rows too, so the per-bill unique index also stops a credit being applied twice. Credits are excluded from ops.v_ap_aging (not payables) and blocked from the single-bill Pay button.

writers.name: vendor-funding:top-up-and-reconcile
external_inputs: Stripe Global Payouts API v2 (financial accounts, inbound transfers, received credits)
QBO Transfer writeback (Chase -> Stripe Vendor Funding)
writers.notes: Vendor Portal Phase 3b (migration 20260820d_vendor_funding.sql). The Stripe payout float and the bookkeeping that mirrors it: QuickBooks holds a BANK account 'Stripe Vendor Funding' (QBO_VENDOR_PAY_BANK_ACCOUNT_ID), funding is a QBO Transfer from Chase (QBO_FUNDING_SOURCE_ACCOUNT_ID, default 72), and every vendor BillPayment is drawn on it (vendor-payments:pay-and-webhook) — so that account's QBO balance should equal the live Stripe balance. Stripe has NO low-balance auto-pull (their bank pull is manual per transfer, US-only, 2-6 business days, 50k/txn · 50k/day · 100k/week), so the threshold top-up is ours: vendor-funding.mjs is SUPERADMIN-only (status / top_up / sync / save_config) and vendor-funding-cron.mjs runs daily — reconcile first, then alert below the floor, or pull to target only when auto_top_up is switched on (ships FALSE; no automatic money movement by default). One ops.vendor_funding_events row per funding event keyed on stripe_object_id, so a Dashboard top-up or a pushed ACH/wire books its QBO Transfer exactly once; a booking failure records book_error and retries. Config rides ops.expense_settings key 'vendor_funding' (multi_writer with brixpense:app). Health: ops.fn_vendor_funding_health() inside fn_sync_health_extra reads the cron's sync_log row (source=vendors sync_type=vendor_funding) for balance/below_floor — red on a failed pull in 7d, settled funding unbooked >24h, or an errored run. DELIBERATELY NOT USED: Stripe's native recurring transfer from the payments balance — brix-order books Stripe payouts as QBO Deposits into Chase 72, and diverting that revenue would break that reconciler.

writers.name: brix-rebates:app-and-rpcs
writers.schedule: on-demand (Refractor -> Pricing -> Rebates tab; staff only)
writers.notes: Rebate Maker (migration 20260821a): per-customer contract rebate programs (first: Starbird / Chicken Coup LLC master agreement, signed 2025-08-25). Programs + rules are edited directly via PostgREST under staff-only RLS (fn_is_staff both directions); rule types volume_growth / ordering_cadence / flat_per_unit / tiered_volume / fixed_per_store, item scope by exact ids + ILIKE name patterns (both empty = matches nothing). Volume is READ from the QBO mirror (qbo_invoices/_lines, parent + subs, Invoices net of CreditMemos) by SECURITY DEFINER ops.fn_rebate_calculate (staff-or-service guard INLINE - not generator-wrapped; keep the guard on any edit). ops.fn_rebate_settlement_create (staff) snapshots the calc into rebate_settlements (partial-unique per program-year) and inserts the Brixpense expense_request (approved + as_bill, tag 'Rebate', bill_number RB-<code>-<year>) - QBO posting stays behind Brixpense's human 'Post to QuickBooks' gate (2026-08-14 rule), hence multi_writer on expense_requests with brixpense + sub-distributors. fn_rebate_settlement_void releases the year + archives the unposted request; refuses once posted. Companion netlify/functions/rebate-report-email.mjs (staff bearer) emails the branded 'Your Alameda Soda rebate is ready' data report from rebates@alamedapointbg.com to operator-chosen recipients and stamps report_sent_at/report_sent_to on the settlement (service role).
